Plato's writing invites readers to question what justice, knowledge, virtue and a good life might mean. This site helps you approach those questions with historical context, explanations of key ideas and paths to the dialogues themselves.

**Start here:** [Beginner's Path](/beginner/why-philosophy.html) · [Explore resources](/resources.html)

## Learning through questions

**Reader:** What makes an action just?

**Guide:** We might begin by asking whether following the law always amounts to doing what is right—and what reasons support an answer.

This exchange is an **illustrative example written for this site**, not a quotation from Plato. In the dialogues, different speakers investigate questions, test definitions and sometimes disagree without reaching a final answer.

## An independent educational project

All the reading guides, articles and resources on this site are free. PLATO is developed independently, with care for sources and for the difference between what Plato wrote and what later readers have made of it.

## Questions or suggestions?

Feedback on a reading guide, translation or historical claim is welcome: [contact@platophilosophy.com](mailto:contact@platophilosophy.com).
